title: BIMAX: A Bitwise In-Memory Accelerator Using 6T-SRAM Structure
problem: SRAM-based in-memory computing has limited operations and unreliable accuracy due to environmental noise and process variations.
motivation: In-memory computing in SRAM is fundamentally fast but limited in functionality and robustness; broader operation support with noise resilience enables wider applicability.
method: BIMAX performs bitwise logic operations (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NXOR) and row-copy directly within 6T-SRAM cells using a specially modified sense amplifier—the circuit normally used to read bits from memory. By designing this sense amplifier with intentional asymmetry (making one input path stronger than the other), it can compute logic results when comparing multiple cell values in parallel, instead of just reading them. The computed results are then written back to memory, enabling logic gates and data copying to happen inside the SRAM array itself.
key_novelty: The core innovation is designing the sense amplifier asymmetrically (with one input path intentionally stronger) so it can reliably compute bitwise logic operations in standard 6T-SRAM cells despite electrical noise.
contributions: 52.7% lower energy dissipation vs state-of-the-art IMC
5.4× improved noise robustness against environmental variations
